newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian iron ore exports set to rise - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Australian iron ore exports set to rise - ABARE.

text.p: Australian iron ore exports are forecast to rise by seven million tonnes to 142 million tonnes in 1997/98 (July-June), the government's key commodity forecaster said on Tuesday.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural Resource Economics (ABARE) estimated Australian iron ore production at 152.0 million tonnes in 1996/97 and 157.0 million tonnes in 1997/98 in its June quarter Australian Commodities publication.
The 1996/97 production estimate is above the 148.5 million tonnes forecast in the March quarter bulletin, and the 1997/98 production estimate has been lifted from 152 million tonnes.
Iron ore export earnings were forecast to rise A$232 million in 1996/97 to A$3.1 billion and to increase to almost A$3.4 billion in 1997/98.
"The forecast of increased earnings in 1997/98 reflects higher export volumes and the modest rise in contract prices negotiated for Japanese fiscal year 1997 (April-March)," ABARE said.

Australian steel exports were forecast to fall to about 2.8 million tonnes in 1997/98, at a value of A$1.35 billion, reflecting the winding down of steel making operations at The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's plant at Newcastle.
